newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-TSCHETTER, MARSHALL LEAD DINAH SHORE AFTER FIRST ROUND.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-TSCHETTER, MARSHALL LEAD DINAH SHORE AFTER FIRST ROUND.

text.p: Kris Tschetter used a hot putter on the back nine Thursday to card a six-under-par 66 and share the first-round lead with Scotland's Kathryn Marshall at the LGPA Nabisco Dinah Shore.
Sherri Steinhauer, Deb Richard and Dale Eggeling were two shots back at 68 after their first tours of the Mission Hills Country Club course in the year's first major championship on the LPGA Tour.
Former Dinah Shore winner Dottie Pepper and Pat Bradley stood at 69, while Briton Laura Davies and Hall of Famer Nancy Lopez were among six players at 70.
Tschetter, who has one victory in nine-plus years on the LPGA Tour, birdied five holes on the back nine by making putts from 20, seven, 15, four and 14 feet.

"I felt I was close to playing some great golf before this," Tschetter said. "But it's hard to play well when you're not making short putts. Three-putting makes the game a lot Tschetter tied for seventh in her previous start and has finished in the top 20 in her last three tournaments.
"Putting has really been a struggle for me the last couple of years," she said.
Marshall opened her round with a bogey, then got her bearings with birdies on the second and third holes. All told, she made seven birdies and one bogey.
"I got off to the worst start possible," said Marshall, who has one victory on her LPGA Tour resume.
"I thought, 'here we go, another bad round.' But I have a lot of confidence in my swing right now."
